# REALTIQ backend needed updates

Audit date: 10 October 2026 (Africa/Lagos). Analysis only. Source implementation findings are not deployment certification.

REALTIQ has substantial reusable backend code: registration/KYC, listings/projects/imports, database search, persistent messaging, payments/cart allocations, escrow disputes/refunds, instalments, title fingerprints and protected sessions, proxy inspection, two tour adapters, trust/reviews, saved alerts and evidence-based valuation/ROI. These are partial foundations for the new specification. The backend is not a scaffold merely because its README says so.

The principal corrections are confidential contact and KYC selfie exposure, current-account authorisation, provider routing and custody, bilateral terms and atomic unit reservation, premature Sold/Owned, normal escrow release without a provider release call, typed unit inheritance/search parity and protected document eligibility. Missing launch modules include Compare, the expanded profile/Partner/agency model, full document issuance, fee/plan/tax/finance engine, social/promotions and ecosystem foundations. No production readiness or complete end-to-end success is claimed.

Original escrow, instalments, maps, verification/trust, proxy inspections, document access/contracts, ROI/automated valuation and core buyer/seller workflows remain original-scope obligations unless a signed change says otherwise. Additional modules and material increments need itemised commercial agreement; reading an audit page is excluded from product scope.

## Methodology, sources and completeness

Located and verified exact documents in both repository roots. Matching SHA-256 hashes show that the sibling copies and backend copies are identical. Read the entire PRD first, including appendices; then Specifications front matter 0.1–0.4 and RQS-01–08; then the entire original Features List Version 2. Independently extracted every page with PyMuPDF, reconstructed tables with the existing PDF tooling, and revisited contents, Appendix A, changes/key decisions, platform rules/glossary, acceptance/edge cases and sections 2.4/14.9/22/26 before reporting. No page has blank extraction.

Missing words are unresolved and must be supplied in a corrected source; full readable coverage cannot be claimed for those portions. The remaining extracted tables and source references are preserved below for review; diagram inspection does not establish any deployed workflow.

The 1,252 frontend AUD records were parsed with their complete expected outcomes, sources, status, evidence, acceptance and scope. Key narrative scope/contradiction/dependency/launch sections were read. Every line of the repeated frontend narrative/checklist was not separately reread. Its frontend findings remain provisional unless explicitly rechecked below. Its repeated generic acceptance and broad classifications are not certified backend facts. Both repositories were inventoried; all backend JavaScript paths/routes/env-name usage were indexed and critical request/auth/validation/persistence/side-effect paths were inspected. This was not a line-by-line review of every one of the 257 source files. Scalar field/runtime coverage is marked limited rather than invented.

## Hierarchy and classification

Detailed RQS governs implementation over the PRD; retain every contradiction in the decision register. The original Features List Version2 is the commercial baseline. A new specification is not a signed expansion of the paid agreement. S1 explicit original scope; S2 professional necessity; S3 ordinary clarification; S4 material expansion; S5 entirely new module; S6 new technical/operational obligation; S7 replacement/reversal; S8 uncertain. Scope proposals are not invoices or legal determinations.

Status vocabulary: **Verified source implementation** means the cited source implements the bounded part; **Implemented but runtime/provider unverified** means an adapter/path exists without authorised integration proof; **Partial** means matching parts plus gaps; **Incorrect** means observed conflicting behavior; **Mock-only** requires affirmative mock-only evidence; **Missing** means no matching complete source capability in the indexed repository, not no external service anywhere; **Externally blocked** requires a known external dependency that cannot be resolved by coding; **Unable to determine** covers unprovided deployments or untested detail. No row is end-to-end verified. Family evidence attached to a granular row is not proof of that scalar's runtime correctness.

Entry points: src/app.js:91 captures raw Paystack callback data before JSON parsing at94; API routers are mounted97–120. index.js connects MongoDB before starting HTTP/Socket.IO and instalment/title-snapshot/marketplace-alert schedulers. src/config/db.js:8–15 creates indexes at startup. Therefore starting the server is not a read-only check and was not done. MongoDB uses MONGO_URI; the cron guide's MONGODB_URI is inconsistent. World Bank scheduler source existence is not proof it is invoked by the entry point. README scaffold and unimplemented-controller claims are stale.

A named route, a controller import or mocked pass does not prove the complete path. Strong reusable bounded parts include upload asset ownership/expiry checks (propertyController407–415), messaging participant access, title view-once compare-and-set, cart-item allocation idempotency key and pending-refund fund blocking. These do not validate all endpoints or production providers.

## Launch feasibility, critical path and shared work breakdown

Today 10October2026 leaves21 calendar days to31October2026; the target has not passed. No staffing/capacity or resolved approval schedule supplied. The current code and missing models do not support a defensible full-scope promise. Do not silently reduce launch acceptance. Replace a date promise with a proof-and-estimation milestone, decisions, integrated acceptance and an agreed capacity-based delivery plan. The frontend audit's12–20 week forecast is provisional and cannot be certified from source inspection.

Critical path: signed custody/fees/legal/identity/field decisions → canonical schema and migration design → bilateral terms/atomic unit state → money ledger/provider proof → document/legal completion → integrated frontend journeys → security/load/restore/UAT → deployment rehearsal. Search/import/Compare/media/social can progress in parallel only after stable common contracts. Adding developers does not resolve provider/counsel approval lead time.

The following **provisional net implementation person-day ranges** describe remaining work after crediting existing code. They are an allowance for joint estimation, not agreed quotation or measured tickets. One person-day assumes6 productive engineering hours. Frontend/backend columns are tasks within one shared package, not duplicate feature quotations. QA/infrastructure are separate. Ranges exclude client/provider waiting, content capture, recurrent costs and audit reading; may change after isolated database/provider proof. Overlapping shared identity/ledger/notification/contract work is charged once in its owning row.

## Non-destructive verification performed and limitations

Inspected package.json scripts and entry points before running anything. No packages installed, lockfiles changed, migrations/seeds/index startup/server run or load test initiated. Temp extraction/read/report tools were used. Existing tests were run from Temp so logger output could not change repository log files; a preloaded guard denied external HTTP/HTTPS/fetch and MongoDB connect/createConnection, while allowing loopback requests used by tests.

Command (working directory Temp):

```powershell
node --require C:/Users/DELL/AppData/Local/Temp/realtiq-be-test-guard.cjs --test C:/Users/DELL/Documents/Samuel-Okiro/RealtiQ/realtiq-backend/test/*.test.js
```

Result: 225 tests across28 files passed;0 failed/skipped/cancelled;duration 51,669.9945ms;exit0. Runtime Node 22.16.0, manifest engine Node 20. This is local logic/schema/mocks/source-regex and limited loopback HTTP/realtime evidence. The safety guard changes available integrations; no database persistence, real custody/settlement/email/SMS/video/deployment was tested. A mocked provider success cannot be labelled operational. No safe unknown-database test was attempted.

Existing historical load artifact, **not rerun**, dated19September2026:1000 concurrent requests in3bursts to localhost5000 /api/projects, one IP and no authenticated writes/sockets. Burst1 802success/198timeouts,P95 successful28,908ms;burst2 204success/792timeouts/4reset,P95~6,775ms;burst3 797success/118rate-limited/85timeouts,P95~19,497ms. Preflight~3,410ms. This fails to demonstrate launch500 concurrent capability or300 ms facets; test conditions/runtime/dataset differ and it does not prove current production performance.

Required next verification, only in separately authorised isolated staging/sandbox: schema/default/conditional field cases; resource/role/seat/revoked-session matrix; real concurrent terms/payment/ledger/refund/release with fault injection; every118 fee acceptance and boundaries; each issuer/doc/access/QR/signature; all four launch tour providers; signed callbacks/authenticity; live channel adapters; OIDC/scopes/mTLS/consent/outbox/replay/DLQ; realistic load,restore,rollback and UAT with both clients. Required acceptance cases are specified per record below. Never exercise production providers or customer data to close this audit.

Confidence: high for exact source defects and successful current local test results; medium for repository absence/architecture gaps and estimated task ownership; low for deployment, licensing, provider approvals, production data, source-clipped language and commercial accepted-history boundaries. Supplied source text was examined, but unreadable/clipped words, entire repeated frontend narrative and all257 files were not completely re-reviewed. Granular records use nearest family evidence and explicitly retain scalar/runtime uncertainty. This report is a comprehensive traceability/action inventory with bounded implementation review, not a certified unique atomic requirement inventory or production launch sign-off.

### Complete specification table-cell register

Reconstructed table rows preserve complete typed dictionaries, quick references, platform rules, glossary, all provider/service/department/document lists, F1–F43, D01–D22 and acceptance tables. This is a source-fidelity appendix, not an implementation count. Field tables specify type, required/default/conditional/value/inheritance/search mapping; all cells must become scalar integration tests. Some apostrophe glyphs are recovered typographically; clipped words are not repaired. Native PDF prose and diagrams remain the governing source for non-tabular edges.

| Specification page | Extracted source cells (ordered) |
|---|---|
| 3 | Code  /  Name  /  What it covers |
| 3 | RQS-01  /  REALTIQ Project Page & Purchase Journey Specification  /  What buyers see and do on a development’s page — from discovery to multi-unit negotiation, checkout and escrow — and what developers manage behind it. |
| 3 | RQS-02  /  REALTIQ Project & Unit Onboarding Specification  /  How a developer sets up a development and its units so that every unit is accurate, searchable and ready to sell. |
| 3 | RQS-03  /  REALTIQ Property Search & Discovery Specification  /  How buyers find property: location search, filters, sorting, map and media controls. |
| 3 | RQS-04  /  REALTIQ Property Listing Onboarding Specification  /  How owners, agents and developers list an individual property, with every field mapped to search and comparison. |
| 3 | RQS-05  /  REALTIQ Property Comparison Specification  /  How buyers compare two to four properties side by side and move straight to enquiring or booking a viewing. |
| 3 | RQS-06  /  REALTIQ User Portals & Dashboards Specification  /  Every signed-in workspace and the shared rules for status labels, payments, viewings, the listing page, documents, finance, trust, promotion and ecosystem readiness. |
| 3 | RQS-07  /  REALTIQ Public Profile Pages Specification  /  What viewers see on the public pages of developers, agencies, owners and partners. |
| 3 | RQS-08  /  REALTIQ Revenue and Monetisation Specification  /  How REALTIQ’s fees are charged, routed, split, invoiced, taxed and refunded. |
| 3 | #  /  Rule  /  Source |

| 3 | 2  /  Everything on the platform. Communication, negotiation, payments and documents stay on REALTIQ. Phone numbers, email  /  RQS-01 section 11; RQS-06 section 1 |

| 5 | Basket  /  The checkout for third-party services, paid as one Moniepoint payment with splits (RQS-06 section 4.1, section 10.4). |

| 8 | User  /  What they need from the project page |
| 8 | Buyers — individual, in Nigeria  /  Location detail, open-house dates, real photos, price and payment options, clear availability, live video viewings when they cannot visit in person. All three buyer groups matter equally. |
| 8 | Buyers — individual, abroad (diaspora)  /  Live video viewings, document requests, currency toggle, clear escrow wording, confidence without visiting. |
| 9 | User  /  What they need from the project page |
| 9 | Buyers — corporate and cooperative; investors and bulk buyers  /  Commercial and residential units; unit comparison, multi-unit enquiry and negotiation, one checkout across several units, per- unit receipts. Corporate and cooperative buyers use team seats; final acceptance of terms is by an authorised signatory (RQS- 06 section 9.1). |
| 9 | Developers (sellers, Developer Portal)  /  Their project’s branding and their own identity; an easy way to present one or hundreds of units; a way to keep prices, availability and progress current; a manageable escrow workload. |
| 9 | REALTIQ staff (REALTIQ Console)  /  Accurate, trustworthy listings; tools to nudge stale projects; escrow operations in the REALTIQ Console to confirm releases and settle disputes. |
| 9 | Independent agents (Partner Portal: Legal, Engineering & Survey, Inspection and Valuation Partners)  /  A separate, limited view of the escrow conditions they are appointed to verify (Sections 14–17). |
| 9 | Buyer’s Agents and Seller’s Agents (Partner Portal)  /  Buyer’s Agents shortlist, attend viewings and negotiate within the buyer’s stated authority; Seller’s Agents manage a developer’s or owner’s listing within the permissions in their mandate (RQS-06 section 9). Both see amounts; neither is neutral, unlike independent agents. |
| 10 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 10 | Features at launch  /  Every feature in this specification is a launch feature.  /  — |
| 10 | Data source  /  Every count, price range, availability figure and status on the page is calculated from unit records; nothing is typed at project level.  /  7.1 |
| 10 | Branding  /  The project’s own logo (or its name as text) leads in the header; the developer’s logo appears smaller in the developer card. REALTIQ’s layout and colours never change.  /  8 |
| 10 | Unit count  /  A project can have one unit or many; the page design is the same. Only the price tile, availability tile, unit section and multi- unit enquiry adapt.  /  2.3, 7.2 |
| 10 | Build stage  /  The eight build stages from RQS-03 drive what the page emphasises; stage can differ per unit or phase.  /  7.3 |
| 10 | Timeline  /  A graphic progress track plus a plain-text Key dates panel, month and year only, for units being built. Revised dates show the original. No calendar grid.  /  10 |
| 10 | Communication  /  All communication stays on the platform; contact details typed into messages are blocked. Enquiries and Messages are separate features.  /  11 |
| 10 | Keeping data current  /  The developer keeps prices, availability and progress current; REALTIQ nudges monthly with a one-button “Nothing has changed” confirmation.  /  19 |
| 10 | Reviews  /  Project reviews and developer reviews are separate systems. Only verified users who bought or almost bought can review; an average appears after 2 qualifying reviews.  /  22 |
| 10 | Unit cards  /  The developer chooses grouped-by-type or individual cards; every unit keeps its own listing page.  /  9.1 |
| 10 | Where purchase starts  /  Payment for a single unit starts on that unit’s listing page; multi-unit purchases start from the multi-unit enquiry.  /  9.2 |
| 10 | Multi-unit buying  /  One conversation, one lead, one checkout for any number of units; offers per unit or as a package total.  /  12, 13 |
| 10 | Negotiating terms  /  The developer sets starting terms per payment type and marks which are negotiable; the buyer accepts, configures within bounds or requests tracked changes. Accepted terms lock into a terms sheet.  /  12.3 |
| 10 | Payment allocation  /  One payment is split across units as fixed before payment; one receipt per unit plus a summary receipt.  /  13 |
| 10 | Payment amount  /  The buyer cannot pay less than agreed; checkout amounts are fixed.  /  13 |
| 10 | Escrow release  /  REALTIQ confirms every escrow release; independent agents verify where appointed.  /  14.4 |
| 10 | Escrow communication  /  Each escrow has a verification room separate from buyer–seller messaging, organised by release condition.  /  14 |
| 10 | Escrow scope  /  The ledger is always per unit; conditions can be per unit, per transaction or shared; each fact is verified once.  /  15 |
| 10 | Disputes  /  A dispute needs a reason and evidence; REALTIQ’s decision within the agreed timeframe is final.  /  16.1 |
| 10 | Dispute threshold  /  Two or more buyers disputing the same shared fact hold every linked escrow; the lower of REALTIQ’s and the developer’s threshold applies.  /  16.1 |
| 10 | Timeframes  /  Maximum times are agreed with REALTIQ and stored with each condition; visible timers and escalation apply.  /  17.1 |
| 10 | Who pays the agent  /  Independent agent fees are paid by the buyer, the seller or both, as agreed in the terms.  /  17.2 |
| 11 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 11 | What agents can see  /  Independent agents see only the conditions they verify and the evidence; never amounts or buyer–seller discussion.  /  14.2 |
| 11 | REALTIQ transaction fee  /  One REALTIQ transaction fee on every sale: a standard rate without escrow and a higher protected rate with escrow; default payer split 50/50, changeable per transaction.  /  13, 17.4 |
| 11 | Stale-listing reminders  /  Monthly reminders, then an amber “Needs confirmation” tag at about 60 days and a banner with checkout paused at about 90 days.  /  19.1 |
| 11 | Stale projects  /  Stale listings are never unpublished or greyed out (grey means Sold); a staleness factor lowers their search ranking.  /  19.1 |
| 11 | Property types  /  All four categories — Flats & Apartments, Houses, Commercial Buildings and Mixed Use — can be sold through a project.  /  2.3, 7.4 |
| 11 | Mixed-use buildings  /  A mixed-use building is sold whole as one listing or as separate component listings; as a project, only a developer can list it.  /  7.4 |
| 11 | Off-platform contact  /  No phone numbers, email addresses or messaging links anywhere.  /  11 |
| 11 | Off-platform exceptions  /  Only live video viewings (run on an outside tool with a REALTIQ-issued link) and one-way notifications leave the platform.  /  11 |
| 11 | Accessibility  /  The page, dashboard and escrow room meet WCAG 2.1 level AA.  /  24 |
| 11 | Street address  /  The full street address is always shown; it carries the Verified badge only once REALTIQ has checked it.  /  11.1 |
| 11 | Verified badge  /  One badge style everywhere, used only on information REALTIQ has verified.  /  20.1 |
| 11 | Build stages  /  Uncompleted building and Semi-finished show a handover date when they will be completed, or “Sold as is” otherwise.  /  7.3 |
| 11 | Escrow  /  Escrow is optional: an extra protection layer on Outright, Instalment or both, chosen by the seller.  /  13, 14 |
| 11 | Master plan and survey  /  The master plan or site plan is always public; the registered survey stays in the private vault and is released on request.  /  6 |
| 11 | Occupancy  /  Every listing declares “Vacant possession” or “Sold with occupiers”; no tenancy terms or income are shown.  /  7.4 |
| 11 | Compare insights  /  Compare counts and price-position insights are available to developers at launch, anonymised and private.  /  18.1 |
| 11 | Portal titles  /  My Portal, Seller Portal, Agency Portal, Developer Portal, Partner Portal and REALTIQ Console. “Landlord” is not used.  /  27.1 |
| 11 | Photo minimum  /  At least 5 photos for Verified status; the number and shot types are Console settings.  /  21 |
| 11 | Media  /  Media is uploaded into dedicated sections by type; renders are labelled “Artist’s impression”.  /  6, 21 |
| 11 | Card labels  /  Cards show Listed By: Developer, Agent or Owner; projects are always “Developer”.  /  2.3 |
| 11 | Compare  /  Any unit can be compared with any other unit of the same category; projects themselves are not compared.  /  7.2, 9.1 |
| 11 | Measurements  /  Square metres only; values in square feet are rejected, not converted.  /  7.5 |
| 11 | Search into projects  /  Search matches units; a project card shows how many of its units match and links to them.  /  23 |
| 11 | Sale prices  /  The reserve price and actual sale price are private and never shown to buyers.  /  5 |
| 11 | Currency  /  Prices are listed in NGN or USD, with an optional second price in the other currency.  /  5 |
| 11 | Team access  /  Every account includes the account holder’s seat; each additional seat is paid. Five standard job types plus custom roles.  /  18.2 |

As individual listings, anyone (owner, agent or developer) can list it; as a project, only a developer account.  /  Both sets of facilities; units grouped by category. |
| 16 | Measure  /  Meaning  /  Example (townhouse in an estate) |
| 16 | Internal floor area  /  Living or usable space across all floors. Required for every unit.  /  240 m² |
| 16 | Built-up area (footprint)  /  Ground the building itself covers. For a building alone on its land, one value. For attached units sharing a lot (for example a 4-unit townhouse block), buyers see both the footprint of their own unit and the footprint of the whole building (all units) — for example “Your unit: 90 m² · Whole building (4 units): 360 m²”.  /  90 m² (unit); 360 m² (whole building) |

| 16 | Unbuilt area  /  Plot size minus built-up area (yards, parking, garden). Calculated automatically so it never contradicts the other two. On a shared lot it uses the whole-building footprint.  /  1,200 m² lot − 360 m² = 840 m² |

| 22 | Participant  /  Can see  /  Can do |
| 22 | Buyer  /  All conditions, evidence, agent reports, decisions and amounts in their own escrow.  /  Comment; raise a concern or dispute; message REALTIQ privately. |
| 22 | Seller (developer or owner)  /  The same, for their side of the transaction.  /  Claim a milestone; upload evidence; respond; message REALTIQ privately. |
| 22 | Independent agent  /  Only the conditions they are appointed to verify, and the evidence for them. They never see payment or transaction amounts, or any discussion between buyer and seller.  /  Accept the brief; request more evidence; schedule a visit; submit a signed report. |
| 22 | REALTIQ escrow officer  /  Everything in the room, plus the payment ledger.  /  Request evidence; approve release; order a refund; decide disputes. |
| 22 | Step  /  What happens |
| 22 | 1. Pending  /  The condition is not yet due. |
| 22 | 2. Claimed  /  The seller says it is met and uploads the evidence the condition requires (for example dated, location-tagged photos, a video walkthrough or a certificate). |
| 22 | 3. Under verification  /  The appointed agent reviews the evidence, visits if needed, and can ask for more. If no agent was appointed, go to step 5. |
| 22 | 4. Agent report  /  The agent submits “met” or “not met”, with reasons. |
| 22 | 5. REALTIQ review  /  The escrow officer carries out REALTIQ’s own due diligence. |
| 22 | 6. Outcome  /  Released (funds go to the seller for that condition and unit); returned for more evidence (back to step 2); or refunded where the terms provide for it. |
| 23 | Step  /  What happens |
| 23 | 7. Disputed  /  Either party contests an outcome. REALTIQ decides within the set timeframe and its decision is final. |
| 23 | Layer  /  Scope  /  Why |
| 23 | Money (ledger)  /  Always per unit.  /  Receipts, refunds, title and handover are unit-specific. This never changes. |
| 23 | Conditions (what must happen)  /  Per unit, per transaction, or shared across a phase or block.  /  Matches how deals are actually agreed. |
| 23 | Verification (checking it happened)  /  Done once, wherever the fact lives.  /  A roof is checked once, not once per buyer. |
| 23 | Condition type  /  Example  /  How it is verified and released |
| 23 | Unit condition  /  “Title perfected for Unit B-07.”  /  Verified for that unit only. Typical for individual sellers and custom requests. |
| 23 | Transaction condition  /  “For these 3 units, release X after 1 year” or “Release when all 3 units are handed over.”  /  Verified once for the whole purchase. The terms say whether release is all together or unit by unit as each is met. Default for bundles: unit by unit; “all together” is negotiable. Amounts are always allocated per unit in the ledger. |
| 23 | Shared milestone  /  “Block A roofing complete.”  /  Verified once; the result flows to every escrow linked to that milestone, across all buyers. |
| 24 | Finding  /  What is held  /  Example |
| 24 | Unit-specific  /  Only the disputing buyer’s escrow for that milestone.  /  “My unit’s roof sheets are damaged.” |
| 24 | Shared fact, weak evidence  /  Only the disputing buyer’s escrow, while REALTIQ checks.  /  A complaint with no supporting material. |
| 24 | Shared fact, credible evidence  /  All unreleased escrows linked to that milestone.  /  New dated photos showing the roof incomplete. |
| 24 | More than one buyer disputes the same fact  /  All unreleased escrows linked to that milestone, automatically.  /  Two buyers report the same problem independently. |

| 25 | Developer milestone board  /  Shared milestones with the number of escrows and buyers linked and amounts awaiting release; a separate queue for unit and transaction conditions; filter by buyer or transaction. |
| 25 | Partner Portal (RQS-06 section 18)  /  Assigned briefs; evidence to review; site-visit scheduling; report submission; history and fees. |
| 25 | REALTIQ Console — escrow operations (RQS-06 section 19)  /  Queue of claims awaiting review, sorted by deadline; flags for overdue or high-value releases; dispute queue; batch release with exceptions list; per-unit ledger reconciliation; two-person approval (one officer prepares, a second approves) for releases or refunds above an amount |

| 28 | Standard job type  /  Can do |
| 28 | Owner / administrator  /  Everything, including adding and removing staff, buying seats, payment templates, escrow and payouts. |

| 28 | Project editor  /  Units, prices, availability, media, progress, key dates and monthly confirmations. |
| 28 | Finance  /  Sales and payments, receipts, instalments and escrow; no page editing. |
| 28 | Viewer  /  Read-only access to the dashboard. |
| 28 | Information  /  Who keeps it accurate  /  How |
| 28 | Prices and price changes  /  Developer  /  Entered per unit or unit type; never typed at project level. Show “Prices updated [date]” and keep a price history so reductions and increases are visible. |
| 28 | Availability  /  Developer, plus automatic updates  /  Developer updates statuses. A unit is marked Sold automatically when its transaction is complete: legal transfer done, escrow fully released and nothing outstanding on either side. |
| 29 | Information  /  Who keeps it accurate  /  How |
| 29 | Construction progress and key dates  /  Developer  /  Milestones, dated media and key dates for the project, groups or units; slipped dates shown as revised, not overwritten. |
| 29 | Counts and ranges on the page  /  System  /  Calculated from unit records (Section 7.1). |
| 29 | Verification and title status  /  REALTIQ  /  Set by REALTIQ’s verification and legal teams, not the developer. |
| 29 | Reviews and questions  /  Verified buyers and users; REALTIQ moderates; developer answers  /  Section 22. |
| 29 | Escrow condition status  /  Verification room workflow  /  Sections 14–17. |
| 29 | Step  /  What happens |
| 29 | 1. Reminders  /  Monthly. Every month the developer gets a dashboard banner and notification asking them to confirm prices, availability and progress, with a one-button “Nothing has changed” confirmation (Section 19.2). Changes that cannot wait for the monthly check are caught by the event triggers in step 2 and by automatic updates (for example units marked Sold when the transaction is complete). |
| 29 | 2. Event triggers  /  Immediate prompt when a milestone’s target month passes without an update, when the handover date passes, or when a buyer reports outdated information. |
| 29 | 3. “Needs confirmation” (about 60 days)  /  After two missed monthly confirmations, the project and affected units show an amber “Needs confirmation · Last updated [date]” tag. This freshness label is separate from availability, so a unit can show “Available” and “Needs confirmation” together. The listing stays fully visible. |
| 29 | 4. Search consequences (about 60 days)  /  A staleness factor lowers the listing in search ranking. In the Property Search & Discovery Specification (RQS-03)’s Recommended sort, the existing “listing recency / freshness decay (+20%)” factor also takes confirmation freshness into account, so a stale listing slowly drops. |
| 29 | 5. Checkout paused (about 90 days)  /  After three missed monthly confirmations, an amber banner appears on the listing: “Details not confirmed since [date] — checkout paused until the developer confirms”, and the affected units stay visible to buyers — they are never unpublished for staleness. Stale listings are no longer greyed out, because grey means Sold. The developer is notified before this happens. Buyers can still view and message, but checkout is paused until the developer confirms, so no one pays for a unit that may no longer be available. |
| 29 | Scope  /  How it works |
| 29 | Whole project  /  One button confirms every unit, the progress track and key dates, and project details. |
| 29 | Group of units  /  Confirm a phase, block or unit type in one step. |
| 29 | Selected units  /  Tick units in the Units grid and confirm them together (bulk). |
| 29 | Single unit  /  Confirm one unit from its row or its edit screen. |
| 29 | All except  /  Update the units that did change, then confirm everything else in one step. |
| 30 | Label  /  What it means  /  Where it appears |
| 30 | Verified seller / developer  /  Sellers and developers need an account and verification before listing.  /  Header and developer card. |
| 30 | Verified listing  /  The listing has been vetted by REALTIQ: identity, authority to sell and on-site photos; development listings also need floor plans, approved building plans and parking capacity.  /  Key facts strip and unit cards. |
| 30 | Verified title  /  Set by REALTIQ’s legal officers, not the seller; once verified, a fingerprint (hash) of the document is recorded with its date and time in a log that cannot be edited, and anyone can check a document against it with its QR code. The hash detects the same document file being uploaded again; detecting the same property listed by several people or sold more than once uses the property register (RQS-06 section 8.4). A public timestamp may be added later.  /  Title and documents section, unit cards. |
| 33 | Area  /  Done when |
| 33 | Quick reference items  /  Every item in Section 1 appears in the stated order, and any item without data is hidden rather than empty. |
| 33 | Consistency  /  Counts, price ranges and availability always match the unit cards; a project with no published units never shows units as available. |
| 33 | Internal statuses  /  “Published” and other internal statuses never appear on buyer-facing pages. |
| 33 | Branding  /  Project logo (or name as text) shows in the header; developer logo shows smaller in the developer card; both name and logo open the developer page. |
| 33 | Unit count  /  A one-unit project shows a single price, “1 of 1 available”, one unit card with Add to compare, and no multi-unit enquiry; nothing else changes. |
| 33 | Build stage  /  The eight official build stages drive the emphasis in Section 7.3; Uncompleted building and Semi-finished show a handover date when they will be completed, or “Sold as is” otherwise; stage can be shown per unit or phase. |
| 33 | Progress and key dates  /  Progress track shows completed, current and upcoming states; each completed step opens dated evidence; the Key dates panel shows launch, start, duration, current and next milestone and handover; revised dates show both original and new target; units or groups with their own schedule show their own track and dates; nothing is shown for completed projects or units. |
| 33 | Unit cards  /  Developer can choose grouped or individual display; large projects have filters, list/table view and paging; sold units are greyed; View details opens the unit listing page; Add to compare works. |
| 33 | Communication  /  No phone numbers or emails anywhere on the page; Message developer, Book a viewing and Request documents all work in-platform. |
| 33 | Multi-unit purchase  /  A buyer can select units (specific or by quantity per type), open one thread, negotiate per unit or one term for all, lock per-unit terms, and pay once at a fixed amount; one receipt per unit plus a summary receipt are issued. |
| 33 | Escrow room  /  A room is created automatically; agents see only their conditions and never see amounts; negotiation messages are not visible in the room; private channels to REALTIQ work; nothing can be edited or deleted. |
| 33 | Escrow at scale  /  A shared milestone claimed once releases to all linked escrows after the objection window, except listed exceptions; each release is recorded per unit. |
| 33 | Disputes  /  Disputes require a reason and evidence; triage outcomes follow Section 16.1; REALTIQ decisions are recorded and final. |
| 33 | Freshness  /  The one-button “Nothing has changed” confirmation works for the whole project, groups and single units, and records a date per unit; monthly reminders, |
| 34 | Area  /  Done when |
| 34 |  /  event triggers, the amber “Needs confirmation” tag, the about-90-day banner with checkout paused, and the staleness ranking factor all work; stale listings stay visible and are never shown grey. |
| 34 | Reviews  /  Only verified users who bought or almost bought can review, with the right badge; project and developer reviews never appear together; the average appears only after 2 qualifying reviews. |
| 34 | Mobile  /  Action bar is fixed on phones; timeline is vertical; unit list view is usable. |
| 34 | Wording  /  All buyer-facing text is UK English, sales-only, and follows Section 21. |
| 34 | Property categories  /  Flats & Apartments, Houses, Commercial Buildings and Mixed Use units each show the details in Section 7.4; no “0 Beds” on commercial units; mixed-use projects group or filter units by category. |
| 34 | On-platform only  /  Phone numbers, emails, messaging handles and outside links typed into messages are blocked, with an explanation to the sender. |
| 34 | Accessibility  /  The page, dashboard and escrow room meet WCAG 2.1 level AA, including the points in Section 24. |
| 34 | Team access  /  An account holder can invite staff, assign a standard or custom role, remove access, and see who did what; seats are counted for billing. |
| 34 | Verified badge  /  The badge appears only on verified information, looks the same everywhere, includes the word “Verified”, shows “Verified by REALTIQ” details on hover or tap, and links to the verification policy. |
| 34 | Seller-developer dashboard  /  Every dashboard area in Section 18 exists and feeds the project page item it supports (Section 1). |
| 34 | Group  /  User types  /  Portal title |
| 34 | Buyers  /  Individual buyer (in Nigeria or abroad); corporate buyer; cooperative buyer  /  My Portal. The page heading shows the account name, for example “Okoro Holdings Portal” |
| 34 | Sellers  /  Individual owner  /  Seller Portal |

| 38 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 38 | Data model  /  Unit-type-first hybrid: unit types generate units; each unit is its own searchable record with effective values (unit → unit type → project).  /  2 |
| 38 | Who creates projects  /  Developer accounts only. Listed By is set automatically to Developer from the verified account.  /  3, 4 |
| 38 | Entry methods  /  Unit-type form, unit cards and a units grid with import all read and write the same records; the developer can switch at any time.  /  2, 5 |
| 38 | One vocabulary  /  Onboarding, bulk grid, import template and buyer filters share one field dictionary with RQS-03 labels.  /  4, 9 |
| 38 | Location  /  State → LGA → Area from REALTIQ’s gazetteer; unlisted areas are matched to the map provider or reviewed. One project pin; unit positions go on the site plan.  /  4, 9 |
| 38 | Build stage and handover  /  Eight build stages; handover is a month and year set once and overridden only where a unit type or unit differs.  /  4 |
| 38 | Amenities  /  The 44-item catalogue, split into estate facilities (S1, marked Delivered or Planned) and unit features (T16). No free-text  /  4 |
| 39 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 39 |  /  amenities.  /  |
| 39 | Measurements  /  Square metres only; values in square feet are rejected, never converted. Plots are not a unit.  /  4, 9 |
| 39 | Prices  /  NGN or USD, optional second price in the other currency; reserve price required and private; actual sale price captured automatically and private.  /  4 |
| 39 | Escrow and fees  /  Escrow is optional and separate from payment type. Payment templates state who pays the REALTIQ transaction fee: buyer, seller or split, default 50/50.  /  4 |
| 39 | Media  /  Dedicated, titled upload sections; each item carries an access level (Free, Paid, On request, Private). The master plan or site plan is always public.  /  4 |
| 39 | Search matching  /  A project matches a search only when one of its units meets every active filter; result cards show matching-unit counts and ranges.  /  6 |
| 39 | Publishing  /  Missing property type, location, price or POA, build stage, availability, off-plan milestone and handover, or residential rooms block publishing; other gaps only limit filters.  /  7 |
| 39 | Scale  /  Hundreds of units: progressive grid loading, background imports and bulk edits with a result summary and one-step undo.  /  5.4 |

| 56 | Case  /  Handling |

A mixed-use building may be listed as a project or not, and sold whole or as components, each with its own listing card |

| 61 | Modality  /  Type / Placement  /  Functional Scope & Operational Mechanics |
| 61 | Location Autocomplete  /  Typeahead / Main Bar & Drawer  /  Hierarchical gazetteer auto-suggest (State → LGA → Area → Gated Estate). Supports multi-token tokenised entry (OR logic) with automated parent absorption and breadcrumb labels to disambiguate identical town / estate names across different states. One control and one shared state between bar popover and drawer. |
| 61 | Property Ref / ID Lookup  /  Exact Input / Drawer Header  /  Direct alphanumeric lookup for a listing reference code (e.g. RQ-10492, RQ-123456, PID). Submitting overrides and pauses all other active filters, location tokens and map bounds without clearing them, isolates the unique listing record and disables sort. An unknown reference shows “No listing with reference X”. |
| 61 | Full-Text Keyword Search  /  Text Index / Drawer Section  /  Case-insensitive scan of listing headlines and descriptions for specialised terms not held as structured attributes (e.g. “penthouse terrace”, “commercial kitchen”). Multiple terms execute with strict AND logic and combine with all other filters. Null bedroom / bathroom counts in commercial stock do not trigger residential exclusions. |
| 61 | Interactive Map Viewport  /  Bounding Box / Map Canvas  /  “Search as I move the map” dynamic viewport querying. Panning or zooming recalculates results to visible coordinate boundaries with a 400 ms debounce. Default: Off (section 6.5); selecting a location token re-centres the map. |
| 61 | Browse by State / Region  /  Taxonomic Chips / Landing Grid  /  Pre-indexed directory landing links and quick-filter chips partitioned across Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT Abuja), for buyers without a specific query. Sets the state parameter and seeds gazetteer context. |
| 61 | Social Feed (Explore & Following)  /  Feed / My Portal  /  Real-estate posts from sellers and third parties (RQS-01 section 27.2): Explore recommends posts by area, property type and topic, and by related listings and liked posts and accounts (RQS-06 section 17.7); Following shows posts from followed accounts. A post tagged to a listing, unit or project opens its page. |
| 61 | Saved Search  /  Signed-in / Bar & Drawer  /  A Registered (signed-in) buyer stores a filter set plus location tokens and map bounds, optionally with new- and reduced- listing alerts (section 6.3). |

| 64 | “Estate” Value  /  Reclassify to listing kind Flag (Single Property _ vs Development)  /  “Estate” is not a physical property type; it represents a development listed by a developer account, with one or more units. It is removed from the property-type enum and handled as a development container flag and via the geographic gazetteer. |
| 64 | Legacy Types: House, Apartment, Commercial, Villa, Penthouse  /  Direct Mapping to 41-Type Structural Enum  /  The current six values migrate into the 41-type enum via listing-management backfill. Listing agents must reclassify records to precise architectural subtypes (e.g. Detached Duplex vs Terraced House or Townhouse). |

They are captured through the Build Stage values “Uncompleted building” and “Semi-finished” applied to the relevant property type, not as a separate property-type value. |
| 64 | Commercial Room Nullability  /  Decoupled Room Query Execution  /  Commercial types may carry null bedroom and bathroom counts. Bedroom, full-bathroom and powder- room (toilet) filters must not exclude commercial listings unless an explicit count is set. |
| 64 | Plot Size Dependency  /  Contextual UI Render Constraint  /  Plot size inputs render for all property types that sit on land; for flats the value is the shared site area. |
| 64 | Filter Label  /  Selectable Values / Range  /  Control Type  /  Dependencies, Mechanics & Operational Defaults |
| 64 | Location Hierarchy  /  State → LGA → Area → Gated Estate  /  Typeahead Multi-Select (OR)  /  Default: All Nigeria. Max 10 concurrent tokens. Selecting a parent node automatically absorbs its child tokens. Parent breadcrumbs disambiguate duplicate place names. Only levels with published data are offered. New areas can be submitted by sellers and join the Area list after a map-provider match or REALTIQ review. Shared between bar and drawer. |
| 65 | Filter Label  /  Selectable Values / Range  /  Control Type  /  Dependencies, Mechanics & Operational Defaults |

| 65 | Travel Radius / Commute  /  15, 30, 45, 60 min from a target pin  /  Single-Select Picker / Dropdown  /  Calls an external traffic-matrix / mapping API to bound results by commute duration from a work or school address. |

Accepts shorthand “25m”, “1.5b”, “500k”.  /  Dual Numeric Text Inputs  /  Values queried strictly in Naira (₦), thousands-separated; USD list prices are converted as set out under Listing Currency & Buyer-Visible Pricing. Validates Max ≥ Min; auto-swaps reversed values with an inline notice. Default: No Min / No Max. |
| 65 | Popular Price Ranges  /  Under ₦25M; ₦25–50M; ₦50–100M; ₦100–250M; ₦250–500M; ₦500M–1B; Over ₦1B  /  Quick-Select Preset Chips (7 Chips)  /  One-tap injection populating Min / Max inputs. Typing directly into Min / Max immediately deselects the active preset chip. |

Conversion uses the Central Bank of Nigeria’s official daily rate (NFEM) from the current or previous day, without altering the query; buyers may manually enter their own FX rate for their displayed conversions. The current “Any Currency” filter is removed. |

Restricts results to listings, including developer projects, that offer REALTIQ escrow, in which the buyer’s funds are held by REALTIQ’s licensed payment partner until the transaction’s specified conditions are met. Requires a new listing-form field. |
| 66 | Filter Label  /  Selectable Values / Range  /  Control Type  /  Dependencies, Mechanics & Operational Defaults |
| 66 | Build Stage Lifecycle  /  Off-plan; Under construction; Uncompleted building; Semi- finished (Advanced Shell / Lock-up); Newly built; Renovated; Previously owned; Old  /  Multi-Select Checkboxes (OR)  /  Default: Any. Unifies physical maturity into 8 lifecycle states, replacing the legacy dual controls (Completion Stage + Listing Type). Semi-finished: exterior fully sealed and secure (lock-up), first-fix plumbing and electrical conduits complete and internal surfaces plastered, with second-fix fixtures, cabinetry, internal doors and decorative finishes not yet installed; distinct from a raw carcass, which is open to the elements. Uncompleted building or Semi-finished listings that will not be completed before handover carry a “Sold as is” label; this is not a separate filter value. Multi-select (buyer filter). |
| 66 | Ready to Move In  /  Boolean Macro Chip  /  Preset Filter Macro  /  Instant macro: sets build stage IN (Newly built, Renovated, Previously owned) in one tap; _ suppresses the handover pickers and the Handover Delivery Stage selector while active. |
| 66 | Handover Delivery Stage  /  Site Preparation & Substructure: Site Clearing & Excavation; Foundation Footing; DPC (German Floor) Carcass: Blockwork / Lintel Level; Decking; Roofing / Parapet Semi- Finished: Lock-up; First-Fix Infrastructure Finishing: POP Ceiling; Tiling & Floor Finishes; Second-Fix Installation; Screeding & Painting Commissioning, External Works & Handover: External Works & Services; Snagging & Inspection; Handover  /  Grouped Multi-Select Checkboxes (OR)  /  Default: Any. Dependent: renders only when “Off-plan” or “Under construction” is active; hidden and cleared otherwise. Identifies the construction milestone a development has reached across five standard Nigerian phases; selecting a phase header selects all of its milestones. These milestones commonly determine when off-plan instalments fall due (the DPC stage is almost always a major payment trigger). Milestone definitions are given below this table. |
| 66 | Handover Delivery Window  /  Handover From (Month / Year) and Handover By (Month / Year)  /  Dual Month / Year Pickers  /  Dependent: renders only when “Off-plan” or “Under construction” is active. Enforces By ≥ From ≥ current calendar month. Month granularity replaces the current day-level completion window. |
| 66 | Bedrooms Boundary  /  Min: Any, 1+, 2+, 3+, 4+, 5+, 6+ Optional Max: Any, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6+  /  Segmented Min + Dropdown Max  /  Default: Any. Minimum sets the lower bound; optional Maximum bounds the upper room count. Enforces Max ≥ Min. Exposed on main bar and drawer. |
| 66 | Exact Bedrooms Match  /  Boolean Toggle (On / Off)  /  Binary Toggle Switch  /  Locks the selected Bedroom minimum into strict equality (e.g. exactly 4) and disables and clears Max. “6+” with Exact matches 6 or more. Inert when Minimum is “Any”. |
| 66 | Full Bathrooms  /  Any; 1; 2; 3; 4; 5+  /  Segmented Pill Selector  /  Default: Any. Evaluates full sanitary suites containing a bath or shower (toilet + bath / shower + basin) as a minimum threshold. Excludes standalone guest powder rooms. Exposed on the bar “Beds & Baths” popover and drawer. |
| 66 | Dedicated Powder Rooms (Toilets)  /  Any, 1+, 2+, 3+, 4+, 5+, 6+  /  Segmented Control  /  Default: Any. Critical Nigerian habitational distinction: captures guest toilets / WCs, usually sited close to the foyer or main living room; the main living lounge and the family lounge may each have their own. Toilets frequently exceed full bathrooms. Drawer only; kept off the bar popover. |

| 67 | Filter Label  /  Selectable Values / Range  /  Control Type  /  Dependencies, Mechanics & Operational Defaults |
| 67 | Built-up Area (Footprint)  /  Min / Max numeric in square metres (sqm)  /  Dual Numeric Inputs  /  Default: No Min / No Max. The ground area the building sits on (its footprint); distinct from Internal Floor Area (total usable internal space) and Plot Size (the land on which the property sits). Validates Max ≥ Min. For attached units on a shared lot, the filter compares the unit’s own footprint; listings also show the whole building’s footprint and the unbuilt area (plot size minus footprint), which are not filters. |
| 67 | Plot Size of Property  /  Min / Max numeric (sqm)  /  Dual Numeric Inputs  /  Visible for all property types that sit on land; for flats the value is the shared site area. Stored and compared in sqm. Helper text: “The land the listed property sits on; the portal does not list land on its own.” |
| 67 | Number of Floors (Terraces)  /  Any; 2 floors; 3 floors; 4+ floors  /  Segmented Control  /  Dependent: visible only when Terraced House or Townhouse is selected; hidden and cleared otherwise. Qualifies terraces, which in Nigeria are built with varying numbers of floors. Requires a new listing-form field. |
| 67 | Furnishing Status  /  Any; Furnished; Semi-Furnished; Unfurnished  /  Segmented Single- Select  /  Default: Any. Standard 3-tier Nigerian habitational furnishing specification. |
| 67 | Serviced Property  /  Any; Serviced; Not Serviced  /  Segmented Single- Select  /  Default: Any. Flags comprehensively managed estates providing centralised security, waste handling, common-area cleaning, power management and facility management with a service charge; aligns with the service-charge ceiling. |
| 67 | Dedicated Parking / Garage  /  Any, 1+, 2+, 3+, 4+, 6+ vehicles  /  Segmented Control  /  Filters private enclosed garages or designated paved compound parking bays. Held as a count filter outside the amenity catalogue; requires a new listing-form field. |
| 67 | Access Road Condition  /  Tarred; Untarred; Flood-prone; Sand-filled area  /  Multi-Select Chips (OR)  /  Default: Any. Describes the condition of the access road serving the property; complements the Paved / Interlocked Access Road and Flood-Free / Covered Drainage amenities. Requires a new listing-form field. |
| 67 | Occupancy Status  /  Any; Vacant possession; Sold with occupiers  /  Segmented Single- Select  /  Default: Any. Identifies whether a property is sold with vacant possession or with occupiers in place. Sold with occupiers means the property has present tenants whose lease or rent is still running; the new owner may keep them, or refund them and evict them. The listing remains a sale; rental tenancies are still not listed. Requires a new listing-form field. Declared on every listing. |

Sponsored (paid) items are labelled in results, capped per page and never bypass filters; their boost is factor (5) of the Recommended sort. |
| 69 | Sort Option  /  Algorithmic Ordering Mechanism & Business Logic |
| 69 | Recommended (Default)  /  Multi-factor relevance score blending five factors: (1) platform verification status, (2) media richness [Photos ≥ 5, Video, 3D Tour], (3) listing recency / freshness decay, where freshness also uses the seller’s last confirmation date, so stale listings drop, (4) profile completeness and (5) active Sponsored boost. Each factor’s weight is a Console setting (RQS-06 section 19.1). Placeholder weights for build and testing: 20% each; REALTIQ sets the live weights in the Console. Changing a weight changes the order without a code change. Sponsored assets never bypass strict user filters. |
| 69 | Price: Low to High  /  Strict ascending numeric sort by current price (₦). Unpriced (POA) listings placed at the end. _ |
| 70 | Sort Option  /  Algorithmic Ordering Mechanism & Business Logic |
| 70 | Price: High to Low  /  Strict descending numeric sort by current price (₦). Unpriced (POA) listings placed at the end. _ |
| 70 | Newest / Most Recent  /  Descending sort by publishing timestamp (created at). Freshly listed properties take precedence. _ |
| 70 | Handover Date: Soonest  /  Ascending sort by projected handover date (handover epoch ASC). Orders off-plan and under-construction inventory by projected completion date; ready / _ existing stock is omitted. |
| 70 | Verified First  /  Boolean tiering: is verified = true first, then sub-sorted by the Recommended relevance score. _ |
| 70 | Recently Reduced  /  Ordered by recency of price reduction (price reduced at DESC). Never-reduced listings placed last. _ _ |
| 70 | Price Reduced: Largest Drop  /  Ordered by absolute or percentage price drop (original price − current price). Isolates highest discount velocity. _ _ |
| 70 | Bedrooms: Most  /  Descending sort by nominal bedroom count. Commercial properties with null bedroom values placed at the end. |
| 70 | Floor Area: Largest  /  Descending sort by internal usable floor space (sqm). Null values sorted to the bottom. |
| 70 | Highest Rated  /  Descending by the average rating received by the seller or developer (RQS-06 section 7.2 Ratings; section 16.2 ratings component); an average exists only after at least two qualifying reviews (RQS-06 section 16.4). Ties are broken by number of reviews, then by the Recommended sort. Listings whose seller or developer has no average are placed after rated ones, in Recommended order. Recommended weights are unchanged. |
| 70 | Trust Tier  /  Ordered by the seller’s or developer’s trust tier (RQS-06 section 16.4): Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze, then New (“New to REALTIQ — building history”, RQS-06 section 16.3). Ties are broken by trust score (0–100), then by the Recommended sort. Accounts whose tier has been removed are placed last, in Recommended order. Recommended weights are unchanged. |

| 71 | Active Filter Chips Bar  /  Media Standards & Listing Badging |
| 71 | Positioned directly below the primary search bar and above result cards. Renders an individual dismissible chip (“x”) for every non-default selection; removing a chip re-queries. Multi-select categories collapse to a group label when more than 3 sub-items are checked (e.g. “5 House Types”). A trailing “Clear All” appears when ≥ 1 filter is active and restores baseline defaults (Available Only, With Photos On, Include Unpriced On) rather than switching them off.  /  Listing cards render explicit badges: photo count (minimum 5 required for verified status, with shot types — completed properties: exterior, living area, kitchen, a bedroom or main room; off-plan: 3 renders plus 2 dated site photos; the number and shot types are settings REALTIQ can adjust), Video badge, 3D Virtual Tour badge (Matterport / 360 viewer) and Floor Plan badge. Verified listings carry a dedicated visual seal. Renders are labelled “Artist’s impression”. Cards also show the Listed By label (Developer, Agent or Owner) and, when a listing is stale, the amber freshness tag. |
| 71 | Interaction Domain  /  Runtime Rule, Behaviour & Edge-Case Protection |
| 71 | Location Typeahead  /  Suggestions fire after 2 characters with a 400 ms debounce, ranked by level (Estate, Area, LGA, State) and listing count. Each row shows its parent lineage (e.g. “Ikate · Lekki · Eti-Osa · Lagos”). Text matching nothing is not applied as a location and offers Keywords instead. |
| 71 | Reference Code Override  /  Submitting an exact listing ID bypasses all criteria, pauses active filters, tokens and map bounds (not clearing them), disables sort and returns the unique |
| 72 | Interaction Domain  /  Runtime Rule, Behaviour & Edge-Case Protection |
| 72 |  /  record with a single chip stating the paused state. Clearing the reference chip restores the prior filter state without reload. |
| 72 | Range Validation & Shorthand  /  Price, floor area, built-up area, plot size and bedroom ranges parse shorthand (“25m” → ₦25,000,000; “1.5b” → ₦1,500,000,000; “500k” → ₦500,000) and enforce Max ≥ Min, swapping with an explanatory inline notice. Nothing applies while a field is invalid. |
| 72 | Exact Bedrooms Match  /  When active, the selected minimum becomes an exact requirement (beds = N) and the Max selector is disabled and cleared. “6+” with Exact matches 6 or more. Inert when Minimum is “Any”. |
| 72 | Dependent Cascade  /  Plan length and deposit render only when “Instalment” is active; the handover window and Handover Delivery Stage render only for Off-plan / Under construction; Number of Floors renders only for Terraced House or Townhouse. Deselecting a parent immediately clears and hides child values, which never contribute to active filter badges. |
| 72 | Zero-Result Diagnosis  /  On zero matches, the engine evaluates individual filter impact and suggests single-tap removals, naming the first that restores results (e.g. “Remove ‘Swimming Pool’ to see 34 homes”). It never blanks the page mid-query and displays a “Save Search & Alert Me” CTA to capture lead intent. See the fallback ladder in section 6.2. |
| 72 | URL Serialisation  /  100% of active filter parameters serialise into the query string, enabling native sharing, browser back / forward traversal, crawler indexation of canonical landing pages and restoration of the last-used state on return. |
| 72 | Server-Side Querying  /  All filtering runs against the full catalogue server-side, not client-side filtering of a pre-loaded set. Shared links without parameters reproduce the same default set. |

| 89 | Area  /  What it does  /  Section |
| 89 | The set  /  One active set per user, 2 to 4 properties, one category (residential or commercial); nothing is added without the buyer confirming  /  2 |
| 89 | Entry points  /  One “Add to compare” toggle on cards, map pin previews, detail pages and project unit cards; “Compare top matches” on search results; a persistent tray; a Compare page with its own URL; “Compare saved properties” on Favourites  /  3 |
| 89 | Manual flow  /  Add, keep browsing, open at 2 or more, review, act (message, viewing, documents), back to results with the exact search restored  /  4 |
| 89 | Criteria-based picks  /  Compare top matches by a chosen criterion with a preview; Compare with similar from one property; Compare with recent sales  /  5, 9 |
| 89 | Comparison view  /  Properties as columns, attributes as rows in collapsible groups; differences only; pin a reference; objective markers only  /  6 |
| 89 | Currency  /  Toggle between NGN and USD with a named daily rate; the buyer can set their own rate; the seller’s price stays the price of record  /  7 |
| 89 | Duplicates  /  Listings of the same property are grouped under one property record; uncertain matches go to review  /  8 |
| 89 | Sold comparables  /  Sold properties of the same category, type and area, with the last asking price; sign-in required for details  /  9 |
| 89 | Status changes  /  Price changes, Under Offer, Sold (greyed), Needs confirmation (amber) and withdrawn listings are handled in place  /  10 |
| 89 | Accounts and leads  /  Full access for guests on the device; sign-in to sync, share or set alerts; enquiries from every column; opt-in lead context; anonymised seller insights  /  11 |
| 89 | Mobile  /  A two-column comparison view; light and dark themes  /  12 |
| 89 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 89 | Set size  /  Minimum 2 to open the view, maximum 4; a full set shows a replace prompt and never drops a property silently.  /  2 |
| 89 | One category  /  A set is residential or commercial, never both; projects are not compared, their units are.  /  2, 3 |
| 89 | No silent adds  /  Every automatic pick goes through a preview and the buyer confirms.  /  2, 5 |
| 89 | One control  /  A single “Add to compare” toggle everywhere; no “compare mode” that turns cards into checkboxes.  /  3 |
| 89 | Markers  /  Objective markers only (lowest price, lowest price per m², largest area); no “best choice” labels; sold properties excluded.  /  6 |
| 89 | FX  /  The Central Bank of Nigeria’s official daily rate (NFEM), set in the Console and refreshed daily; sellers cannot change the rate buyers see.  /  7, 16 |
| 89 | Sale prices  /  The actual sale price is never shown; sold comparables show the last asking price before sale.  /  9 |
| 89 | Sign-in gate  /  Sold details need sign-in (Registered level); guests see a count.  /  9, 16 |
| 89 | Similarity  /  ±20% size and ±15% price by default; the buyer can adjust them.  /  5, 16 |
| 89 | Occupancy  /  Every listing declares Vacant possession or Sold with occupiers; no occupier income is shown.  /  6, 16 |
| 90 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 90 | Launch scope  /  Every Compare feature launches, including the top navigation tab. Compare with recent sales appears once an area has the minimum number of sold records set in the Console.  /  14 |
| 97 | Area  /  What it covers  /  Section |

| 97 | Seller portals  /  Shared core for Seller, Agency and Developer Portals, plus agency and developer additions and their public pages  /  7 |
| 97 | Listings  /  Location entry, prices and sale data, Listed By display, media from any provider, archive not delete  /  8 |

| 97 | Trust  /  Verification versus trust score and tier; components by role; visibility; tiers and blacklist  /  16 |
| 97 | Promotion  /  Sponsored and Featured; paid products; Promote page; packages and prepaid bidding; reporting; Explore ordering  /  17 |

| 97 | Notifications and legal explainer  /  Channels and categories per profile; plain-language legal terms  /  20, 21 |
| 97 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 97 | Scope  /  Sales of residential, commercial and mixed-use property only; no rentals, leases, short lets or land anywhere.  /  1 |
| 97 | On-platform only  /  Communication and payments stay on REALTIQ; phone numbers and emails are never shown to another party.  /  1 |
| 98 | Topic  /  Decision  /  Section |
| 98 | Profiles  /  One email can hold one buyer profile, any number of seller-side profiles and partner profiles; each keeps its own records.  /  2.2 |
| 98 | Plans and seats  /  Developer, Agency and Partner profiles can be required to hold a paid plan; listing is free for owners within a Console cap. Every account includes the holder’s seat; each additional seat is paid.  /  2.2, 4.7 |
| 98 | Status labels  /  Public labels are Available, Under Offer and Sold; Sold only when legal transfer is complete, escrow fully released and nothing is outstanding. Freshness is a separate label.  /  5 |
| 98 | Public counts  /  Enquiries, viewings, negotiations, views and saves are shown on listing and project pages; never on profile pages; never with identities.  /  5.4 |
| 98 | Escrow  /  An optional protection layer on Outright, Instalment or both; funds held in a Moniepoint segregated account; REALTIQ instructs releases.  /  10.1, 10.4 |
| 98 | Payment routing  /  Property payments and the services basket go through Moniepoint with splits; Paystack only for plans, subscriptions, promotion and REALTIQ fee invoices. No stored balance except a single-campaign promotion budget.  /  10.4 |
| 98 | REALTIQ transaction fee  /  One fee on every sale; standard rate without escrow, protected rate with escrow; default payer split 50/50.  /  10.2 |
| 98 | Media access  /  Photos, renders, recorded video tours and a development’s master plan or site plan are always Free; REALTIQ receives the whole fee for Paid items.  /  13 |
| 98 | Documents  /  REALTIQ never issues documents in another party’s name; every document carries the REALTIQ mark and verifies by QR code.  /  14.2 |
| 98 | Trust  /  One Verified badge for checked facts; a separate trust tier; no negative labels; only platform-completed transactions count.  /  16 |
| 98 | Promotion  /  Sponsored is labelled and never bypasses filters; Featured is editorial with no ranking weight; bidding needs a minimum quality score.  /  17 |
| 98 | Partner payment terms  /  Partners choose from REALTIQ-approved, switchable payment-term types; REALTIQ’s platform rate is included in the partner’s price.  /  18.5 |
| 98 | Console  /  Prepare-and-approve for sensitive actions; nobody approves their own work; reserve prices are never visible to staff.  /  19.3 |

| 111 | Area  /  Settings |
| 111 | Outright  /  Price; whether a reservation deposit is allowed and its amount; days allowed to pay the balance; which terms are negotiable |
| 111 | Instalment  /  Minimum deposit; longest period; allowed frequencies; schedule template, optionally linked to construction milestones; grace period; penalty rate and method; default threshold; default remedy; which terms are negotiable |
| 111 | Escrow  /  Which payment types it covers (Outright, Instalment or both); release conditions; independent agents required; objection window; timeframes |
| 111 | Currency  /  List price in NGN or USD. Terms may state “listed in USD, payable in NGN at the rate agreed on the day of payment”: before each NGN payment one party proposes a rate and the other confirms it in the platform; the checkout is created only from a confirmed rate, which then cannot change. The Console FX source is shown for reference. Fees are calculated on the naira actually paid; receipts show the USD figure, agreed rate and NGN paid (RQS-08 Section 7.3) |
| 111 | REALTIQ transaction fee  /  Every sale pays one REALTIQ transaction fee: the standard rate without escrow and the protected rate on any part under escrow. Payer: buyer, seller or split; the default is split 50/50 and can be changed for each transaction. The fee is shown on the terms sheet before terms lock (RQS-08 Section 7) |
| 111 | Refund and cancellation  /  One of: full refund; refund less a stated percentage; seller’s choice within a REALTIQ cap; a seller-defined refund schedule. REALTIQ’s transaction fee is non- refundable once terms lock and the innocent party never bears it: the party at fault pays the whole fee and the innocent party is refunded in full; on mutual cancellation each pays its own share; on a no-fault reversal REALTIQ keeps a cost-recovery portion split equally, or waives it. No REALTIQ fee is charged on penalties or forfeited deposits (RQS-08 Section 7.2) |
| 111 | REALTIQ thresholds  /  Optional. REALTIQ can set maximum penalty rates, minimum grace periods and refund floors in the Console, and can switch them on or off. A seller can choose to list within them; such listings show a “REALTIQ Standard Terms” label |

| 131 | Technical  /  Platform running and secure  /  System health; ecosystem connectors (Section 23); integrations (Moniepoint, Paystack, Mapbox, Zoom, Termii, Postmark, Firebase Cloud Messaging, CBN FX feed, address verification, SMS/WhatsApp, e-signature); incidents; feature switches; staff access; security alerts  /  Production changes; access grants |

| 136 | Requirement  /  What REALTIQ provides |
| 136 | Global identifiers  /  A global participant ID for every account and a global property ID for every project, unit and listing. Both are independent of REALTIQ, permanent and never reused; REALTIQ’s own listing references remain for display. A cross-reference table maps each ID to the matching record in any connected application. |
| 136 | Identity and roles  /  One account holds several roles and profiles (Section 2). REALTIQ’s identity service supports OpenID Connect, so the same account can later sign in to connected applications. Identity details pass to an application only with the user’s consent. |
| 136 | Verification records  /  Each verification result (identity, company, licence, title, rating, trust tier) is stored as a record with its source, issue date and expiry (Sections 3 and 16), so it can be reused later. |
| 136 | Payments  /  All money movement goes through the payments abstraction layer (RQS-08 section 13). Escrow funds stay with REALTIQ’s licensed payment partner (Section 10.1). |
| 136 | Notifications  /  Every notification goes through one notification service with channel adapters (in-app, email, SMS, WhatsApp, push), following each user’s preferences (Section 20). |
| 136 | Events  /  REALTIQ publishes its own events through a transactional outbox from launch, even before anything subscribes: listing.created, listing.price changed, _ listing.withdrawn, offer.accepted, transaction.completed, property.handover, project.created, unit.status changed, milestone.verified and title.verified. Delivery is at _ least once; each event carries an idempotency key, the global property ID and the participant IDs involved. |
| 136 | Webhooks  /  Approved subscribers receive events by webhook. Each delivery is signed (HMAC-SHA256); failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff for 24 hours, then move to a dead-letter queue shown in the Console. |
| 136 | Partner APIs  /  Versioned REST APIs described in OpenAPI 3.1 for listings, property records, participant profiles and transaction status. JSON bodies; timestamps in UTC (ISO 8601); amounts in minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code; areas in m². New optional fields may be added within a version; removing or changing a field needs a new version, and the previous version stays supported for at least 12 months. |
| 136 | Service authentication  /  OAuth 2.0 client credentials per connected application, scoped to its contract, over mutual TLS. Credentials sit in the platform secret store and rotate at least every 90 days. |
| 136 | Consent and data sharing  /  Users approve, per connected application, what data is shared, in Settings › Connected applications, and can withdraw approval at any time. Every share is logged with time, application, purpose and consent version, in line with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. |
| 136 | Deep links  /  Stable links open a REALTIQ listing, property record or transaction in context. REALTIQ’s own sign-in and access checks apply on arrival. |
| 136 | Source labels  /  Every record and media item carries its source (REALTIQ or a named connected application) and the time it was received. Buyer-facing views label external content by source. |
| 136 | Sandbox  /  A sandbox environment where a connected application can be tested against REALTIQ’s contracts before it is switched on. |
